# HistogramChart

**Class:** `UltraCanvasHistogramChart` · **Group:** [Charts](../Groups/Charts.md) · **Header:** [`UltraCanvas/include/Plugins/Charts/Engine/Charts/UltraCanvasHistogramChart.h`](../../../UltraCanvas/include/Plugins/Charts/Engine/Charts/UltraCanvasHistogramChart.h) · `#include "Plugins/Charts/Engine/Charts/UltraCanvasHistogramChart.h"`

**Inherits:** [`UltraCanvasChartEngineElement`](UltraCanvasChartEngineElement.md) → [`UltraCanvasChartElementBase`](UltraCanvasChartElementBase.md) → [`UltraCanvasUIElement`](UltraCanvasUIElement.md) → `Element`

## What it is for

A picture's histogram: how many pixels have each level of red, green and blue (overlaid or one channel) or luminosity, beside a photo

The component documentation with explained, compiled C++ examples:

## Creating it

Factory functions (the usual way - every element is held in a `std::shared_ptr`):

```cpp
std::shared_ptr<UltraCanvasHistogramChart> CreateHistogramChart( const std::string& id, int x = 0, int y = 0, int w = 0, int h = 0);
```

Constructors:

```cpp
UltraCanvasHistogramChart(const std::string& id, int x = 0, int y = 0, int w = 0, int h = 0);
```

The first string argument is always the element's **identifier**, never its text (see [Core concepts](../Core-Concepts.md#identifiers)).

## Callbacks

Assign a lambda to the member (or call the setter). Capture the element and its parents **raw**, never as a `shared_ptr` - see [Events and callbacks](../Events-and-Callbacks.md#ownership).

| Callback | Signature | When it fires |
|---|---|---|
| `onLevelHover` | `std::function<void(int level)> onLevelHover` | A level is hovered or left (-1). |

## Option types in this header

### enum `HistogramDisplay`

What the histogram shows.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Combined` | red, green and blue overlaid, each in its own colour |
| `Red` |  |
| `Green` |  |
| `Blue` |  |
| `Luminosity` | the brightness of each pixel (Rec. 601 luma) |

### enum `HistogramScale`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Linear` |  |
| `Logarithmic` | tall spikes no longer flatten the rest; empty levels stay at zero |
